documents.title: Royal Cork Yacht Club Keelboat Racing Course Card, 2026 update
documents.why: The card itself: forty numbered courses as rounds with cumulative distances under wind headings, the notes that the General Sailing Instructions say form part of them, and the card's own description of its two starting and finishing lines. Published on the club's Keelboats Notice Board. The sidecar leaves out page 1, the chart: its labels overlap ("COURSE CARD UPDATE 2026" is set twice over itself) and pdftotext splits them differently from one poppler version to the next, so a sidecar of that page would not reproduce in CI; nothing on it is text a reader needs.

documents.title: General Sailing Instructions for Royal Cork Yacht Club Keelboat Racing 2026
documents.why: 22.1 makes the card the round-the-cans course list; 22.3 gives the only positions the club publishes, for the Port of Cork's four permanently laid race marks; 26 defines the start and finish lines every course begins and ends at.

addMarks.why: The instructions position four marks; the card names twenty-six more. The numbered channel buoys and the E, W, EF and C buoys are Port of Cork navigation marks: charted, but given a position in no official document, no Cork Week instruction of any year, and no Port of Cork publication found — the port's Information Manual and passage plans name them and place none, and the NGA List of Lights (Pub. 114) carries Cork Harbour's shore, range and pier lights but not one channel buoy. Nineteen of them are positioned from eOceanic's list of Irish marks, which names each by its number — see `buoys`; their entries here carry only an id and a name. E4, a north cardinal, is positioned from Pat Tanner's Cork Harbour workbook: a geotagged photograph of the buoy, which a Navionics reading puts 6.9 m off and a B&G Vulcan reading 0.9 m off. It is preferred to eOceanic's E4, 23 m away and 24–30 m from both plotter readings. OpenStreetMap, where all twenty were first traced and numbered by eye against the chart, is now the cross-check in `checks`; its E4 is 16 m from the photograph's. Cage is placed from neither: buoy C1 is not in OpenStreetMap — the nearest node to it is 850 m away — and the club supplied its position directly, so it is carried as club correspondence; eOceanic's C1 is 39 m from it, corroboration rather than a better authority for the mark the club's own line is laid to. It is the Grassy Walk line's outer distance mark, and with it placed the line's geometry checks out: solving for the start line that best fits the card's own printed distances over 28 courses lands 321 m from the midpoint of the line between Cage and the club, which is corroboration of Cage, of the numbering and of both at once. EF2 is placed as the club gave it, 51° 50.631' N 8° 14.238' W, the same footing as Cage; eOceanic's EF2 is 49 m from it and a Navionics reading by Pat Tanner 15 m. EF4 was not identified, and keeps its placement and no position. OpenStreetMap's three East Ferry nodes, once taken for the EF buoys, are not them: the nearest is 571 m from EF2. Dutchman and Curlane are laid marks the card places in words; White Bay the card only names.

marks.name: Harbour navigation buoy E4
marks.source: Pat Tanner, Cork Harbour workbook v3.19 (github.com/Bateleur88/cork-harbour-orc): a geotagged photograph of the buoy, confirmed within 7 m by Navionics and B&G Vulcan readings, 29 September 2026

marks.name: Harbour navigation buoy EF4
marks.placement: A Port of Cork navigation buoy, charted (Admiralty 1777) and maintained by the port; the club publishes no position for it, and none was found in any port publication. Its position is a race-day fact until one is.

marks.name: Dutchman
marks.placement: The Dutchman mark will be a ‘laid’ club racing mark positioned approx. 2 cables SE of the Dutchman Rock/Fennels Bay.

marks.name: Curlane
marks.placement: “Curlane” will be a mark laid on the Curlane Bank.

marks.name: White Bay
marks.placement: Named by course 73 only; the card says nothing of where it is beyond its name, White Bay being the bay on the harbour's east shore north of Roches Point.

buoys.citation: eOceanic's list of Irish marks (eoceanic.com/weather/ireland, 5 October 2026)
buoys.why: eOceanic, a cruising-guide site, lists Ireland's buoys and lights by name with positions to a thousandth of a minute and their light characteristics, and names every channel buoy the card uses by its number. It does not say where its positions come from. It is preferred to OpenStreetMap, which these buoys were first traced from, because it is a document that numbers them — the numbering was otherwise our own reading of the chart — and because Pat Tanner's Cork Harbour workbook (github.com/Bateleur88/cork-harbour-orc), whose depth tests for the passages in #16 were run against these positions, takes its buoys from it. E4 is not taken from it: see the manifest's addMarks.

artifacts.why: A course is its rounds run together, from the start line to "Finish", which is the same line (26); the rounds, with the cumulative distance each closes at, are where the race officer may shorten it and are carried as the card's first note. Courses 76 and 81 cross the finishing line laid at Cage at the end of their first round and sail on: that crossing is an entry passing Cage. Course 23 prints no distances. The blue dot some course numbers carry on the printed card is a graphic and is not read.

startLine.why: 26 lists the lines that may be used — the Grassy Walk line to Cage or a laid mark, and a committee-vessel line — and each is also the finish, so every course ends at SL.

items.why: The buoys were first positioned from OpenStreetMap, independently of eOceanic and of the photograph E4 is placed from, and numbered by eye against the chart. Two independent readings of one buoy field should agree to within a buoy's swing and the imagery's registration; seventeen of the twenty are within 60 m. The three below are further apart and are recorded as such: which reading is nearer the buoy is not known, and eOceanic's is the one carried.

expected.No.9: the nearest eOceanic buoy to the trace all the same; the next, No.11, is 428 m from it
expected.No.6: the nearest eOceanic buoy to the trace all the same; the next, No.3, is 451 m from it
expected.W1: the nearest eOceanic buoy to the trace all the same; the next, W2, is 324 m from it

items.why: Under IALA region A the harbour's odd-numbered buoys are starboard hand, green, and its even-numbered ones port hand, red — which the card's own Cage, C1, settles as green. Each row eOceanic is read from must name the mark's number and give a light of the matching colour, so a row taken for the wrong buoy is caught.

Cage and EF2 are placed from the club's correspondence, and eOceanic lists both — C1 by that name, EF2 as "Cork Harbour east channel" with EF2 in its light. The club's figure is carried, for the marks of its own racing; eOceanic's should agree with it to within a buoy's swing. eOceanic prints "C1" twice, the other off the Essex coast, so the row nearer the mark is the one compared.
